paragraphs.text: Cornelia de Lange syndrome-4 (CDLS4) is a cohesinopathy caused by mutation in RAD21, which encodes a structural protein of the cohesin complex. Affected individuals have growth retardation, minor skeletal anomalies, and facial features overlapping those of Cornelia de Lange syndrome (CdLS), but cognitive impairment is much milder than in classic CdLS (Deardorff et al., 2012). Krab et al. (2020) described the phenotype as an attenuated form of CdLS compared with that caused by NIPBL or SMC1A variants, especially for facial morphology, limb anomalies, cognition, and behavior. Some patients have holoprosencephaly (Kruszka et al., 2019; Goel and Parasivam, 2020).

paragraphs.text: Krab et al. (2020) reported 49 individuals from 33 families with RAD21 alterations, 24 of whom had not been reported previously. The patients came from Australia, Europe, Turkey, Canada, and the United States. Full clinical information was available for 29 patients from 22 families (cohort A). Their phenotype was an attenuated form of CdLS compared with that caused by NIPBL or SMC1A variants, especially for facial morphology, limb anomalies, cognition, and behavior. The 29 patients in cohort A were aged 0 to 61 years, and 15 were male. All had CdLS scores of at least 5. Common features included short nose (23/26), long and/or smooth philtrum (26/29), concave nasal ridge (24/29), thick eyebrows (20/24), long eyelashes (21/26), synophrys (19/28), short fifth finger (23/28), and postnatal microcephaly (16/28). No patient had a major limb malformation. Small hands (5/27), small feet (3/27), hirsutism (10/26), seizures (2/22), and visual impairment (0/24) were less frequent than in the NIPBL and SMC1A cohorts. Hearing loss occurred in 8 of 24 patients, heart anomalies in 9 of 23, gastroesophageal reflux in 13 of 25, and cleft palate in 6 of 25.

paragraphs.text: Krab et al. (2020) summarized the natural history. Pregnancy and birth usually progressed normally, and prenatal growth retardation was uncommon. About half of the patients had congenital anomalies such as cleft palate or cardiac anomalies. Diaphragmatic hernia, anal atresia, and choanal atresia occurred occasionally. Short stature and microcephaly developed postnatally. Vertebral anomalies (clefts and hemivertebrae) and malformations of structures derived from the embryonic foregut were unusual findings, but they were relatively frequent in this series.

paragraphs.text: CDLS4 is transmitted as an autosomal dominant trait. Mutations can arise de novo (Gudmundsson et al., 2019; Krab et al., 2020) or be inherited. Minor et al. (2014) reported the first familial case, in which a RAD21 deletion was inherited from the mother, and discussed variable clinical presentation within families and low penetrance. Boyle et al. (2017) found a RAD21 deletion in an index patient with mild CdLS as well as in the patient's mother and 2 aunts, who did not meet CdLS diagnostic criteria. They suggested that RAD21 variants are associated with incomplete penetrance and that carriers may therefore be underdiagnosed. Krab et al. (2020) found that RAD21 variants were frequently familial: this was the case in 9 of 21 index cases in which inheritance could be determined.

paragraphs.text: McBrien et al. (2008) used oligo array CGH to characterize a small 8q24.1 microdeletion in a boy with a mild Langer-Giedion-like phenotype. The deletion involved EXT1 alone and not TRPS1, and the authors suggested that this pointed to a functional disturbance of TRPS1. The boy also had unusual features, including prominent toe pads and fat pads on the soles of the feet, similar to those described in Pierpont syndrome.
